nodes.label: ADR-001: No build step; ship pinned CDN ES modules
nodes.rationale: No npm/bundler/package.json; Three.js pinned to three@0.160.0 via a CDN import map, relative paths, explicit .js extensions. Self-contained payloads must run with zero toolchain, work offline after first fetch, stay reproducible; rejected Vite/Webpack, @latest, and the UMD global. ES modules require HTTP (file:// fails); local serving is XAMPP Apache on port 8080.

nodes.label: ADR-002: Host integration via a window.simAPI global, not postMessage
nodes.rationale: Sim runs in a sandboxed iframe exposing window.simAPI (pause/resume/reset) plus a static four-field meta.json; deliberately no postMessage/window.parent/window.top. Smallest possible contract, no async plumbing; in-sim Reset must route through simAPI.reset() (one reset path only).

nodes.label: ADR-003: CSS design tokens are the single runtime source of truth for all visual values
nodes.rationale: Every colour/radius/spacing is a CSS custom property read live at runtime via getComputedStyle; no hex literals in JS or component CSS. One visual language across subjects; a re-theme is a token swap; enforces the named rules at a single chokepoint.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Every geometry change funnels through one rebuild() pipeline
nodes.rationale: A single rebuild(shapeData) in fixed order (dispose -> resolve angles -> generate mesh -> seat -> analyze edges -> draw projections -> place labels -> notify) is the only geometry path. Prevents WebGL context exhaustion/leaks in the iframe and guarantees consistent state; the orchestrator that owns it grows large.

nodes.label: ADR-005: Re-derive every ported sign visually (Unity LH -> Three.js RH), explicit ZXY Euler
nodes.rationale: Magnitudes port unchanged but every sign is re-derived visually against a worked square-pyramid; Euler order pinned ZXY (Unity's) in iShape.applyShapeTransform. Copying Unity's negative signs verbatim yields plausible-but-wrong mirrored/back-to-front projections; Three.js default XYZ would silently change rotations.

nodes.label: ADR-006: Fat lines + hard-edge geometry + quantized edge welding for crisp technical linework
nodes.rationale: Linework uses LineMaterial + LineSegments2/Line2 fat lines, hard-edged non-indexed geometry, and meshAnalyzer welds endpoints at 1e-3 tolerance. LineBasicMaterial caps at 1px on most GPUs; welding stops double lines on curved-solid rims. Requires resolution sync, computeLineDistances(), and polygonOffset.

nodes.label: ADR-007: Orchestrator + leaf modules; leaves don't cross-import, only genericSolid is shared
nodes.rationale: Module 2 is one orchestrator (main.js) owning scene/state/rebuild plus single-purpose leaf modules that do not import each other; only genericSolid.js (stateless polygon trig) may be imported by siblings. Keeps the dependency graph a star so a leaf can be replaced without tracing sibling webs; the orchestrator absorbs all wiring and grows large.

nodes.label: ADR-008: Rotation priority hierarchy enforced through mutually-exclusive UI
nodes.rationale: Precedence Face-Inclination HP/VP > Orient-to-Corner/Edge preset > Manual Y, a higher mode disabling the lower via uiManager toggles. Prevents contradictory orientation and teaches concepts in order; preset angles are square 45, triangular 30, pentagonal 54 (not 18), hexagonal 30.

nodes.label: ADR-009: No shared code library; topic clones are manual full copies simplified from Module 2 (the master)
nodes.rationale: No shared library or sync tooling; Module 2 is the master and each graphics_module_2_topic_* folder is a full copy simplified via a single ENABLED_TIERS flag. Improvements are backported as merges, not blind copies. Keeps each topic a standalone deployable payload; the copies WILL drift (the deliberate cost).

nodes.label: ADR-010: DESIGN.shared.md is the platform-wide visual contract, duplicated per module (interim)
nodes.rationale: The platform visual system was extracted into DESIGN.shared.md, meant byte-identical per module with only a module-local appendix. Per-module duplication accepted only as interim because no shared Simatrix root existed yet. Superseded by ADR-022 once the root existed and the copies had drifted.

nodes.label: ADR-011: Module 1 uses a shared engine.js + thin pages, a different architecture from Module 2
nodes.rationale: Module 1 shipped seven thin HTML pages calling one shared engine (src/engine.js, initSim) over shared shell.css, structurally different from Module 2's orchestrator + leaf modules. Fit its simpler 2D points/lines geometry and stopped the seven pages from drifting. Fully superseded by ADR-033 (partially first by ADR-029).

nodes.label: ADR-012: On-demand Compare View replaced the persistent dual-pane (PiP + toggle bar + swap())
nodes.rationale: Points/Lines dropped the persistent PiP dual-pane; the main pane is always the live 3D scene (#c3d) and the second view appears on demand in a floating Compare card showing a live-rebuilt (never snapshot) view. swap()/isMain3D() survive as no-op shims. Introduces the no-transform invariant on #sim-viewport/#canvas-area/body.

nodes.label: ADR-013: The fold camera moves, overturning 'camera never moves during the fold' (then revised)
nodes.rationale: Overturned the old hard rule; the fold now animates the camera. First replacement (perspective->ortho front-on morph) was replaced by a held-angle dolly (animateFoldHold), which read as a bottom-right swoop and hid the hinge. The held-angle revision is itself fully overturned by ADR-036; the first reversal (camera does move) still stands and must not be re-cited as 'camera never moves'.

nodes.label: ADR-014: Auto-zoom is a one-shot eased dolly; a rebuild does tight-fit XOR push-back, never both
nodes.rationale: Ported Module 2's clip-aware auto-zoom (reframeIfClipped at end of rebuild, push-back only): a per-rebuild one-shot fixed-duration eased dolly, and a rebuild does either a fresh tight fit (boot/reset) or the push-back (slider edits), never both. Replaced a per-frame exponential follow that lurched; needs an accurate contentBox, not the full grid.

nodes.label: ADR-015: Self-check is +/-0.5-tolerant, never auto-fills, OR-arrays only for degenerate cases
nodes.rationale: The Problem Library self-check compares dialed values to a target with +/-0.5 tolerance and never auto-fills (loading a problem resets to defaults; the student dials, the check lights green). OR-array targets are allowed only for genuinely degenerate geometry. theta=+/-theta and endpoint A/B ORs were rejected as false positives that green a wrong drawing.

nodes.label: ADR-016: Drawing line conventions follow N.D. Bhatt / ISO
nodes.rationale: Foot/point markers are thick filled dots (paper halo + colour disc); 2D orthographic projectors are solid Type-B continuous thin; 3D pictorial projectors stay dashed. Corrected an earlier 45-degree x foot and solid-VP-in-3D choice. In 2D the HP/VP distinction is carried by position, so solid is standards-correct (N.D. Bhatt); 3D keeps the Two-Cue Rule (HP solid-teal / VP dashed-amber).

nodes.label: ADR-017: The Lines sim is a 5-step problem-solving stepper, not six fixed-orientation cases
nodes.rationale: Restructured to a 5-step build-up on one general line (True Length -> distances -> inclinations theta/phi -> orthographic projections -> traces), all pinning LineCase.INCL_BOTH, with dedicated per-step controls (not cumulative). Teaches the process of constructing views; problem targets dropped case and pin explicit theta/phi. Viewport labels 'line AB'/'end A' are hard-coded.

nodes.label: ADR-018: Favor textbook fidelity over fudging; reconcile units by a declared scale (1 unit = 10 mm)
nodes.rationale: When a textbook problem does not fit existing controls, add a geometrically-correct control + a per-problem hint rather than fudge a number or drop it. Textbook wording is verbatim; units reconciled by a declared scale 1 world unit = 10 mm, a per-sim label change (Points/Lines show mm, pointData.js stays cm) not a world rescale (toW(v)=v/10 unchanged).

nodes.label: ADR-019: Verify sims headlessly via Node's built-in WebSocket CDP; no puppeteer, no npm
nodes.rationale: End-to-end verification drives headless Chrome over the DevTools Protocol using Node's built-in WebSocket/fetch (swiftshader software WebGL, cache disabled), never puppeteer/playwright/npm. The final green check must run the shipped module, not a hand-typed replica (a replica once passed while the real module had a call-site bug).

nodes.label: ADR-020: 'Simple Positions' carries no topic number, and the folder names hide the master
nodes.rationale: Two naming choices: the Simple Positions clone's human-facing title carries no topic number (user preference), and deploy copies are named graphics_module_2_topic_* which do not reveal they are copies of the master. A newcomer cannot infer the master->deploy relationship from the directory listing (known issue).

nodes.label: ADR-021: The Lines expanded Compare enters a workbench, true 50/50 with docked live parameters
nodes.rationale: On the Lines side-by-side Compare, collapse the step wizard and re-parent the driver controls (TL, distance HP/VP, theta, phi) into a docked #workbench-rail spanning both panes, gated by cfg.workbenchControls. The reserved wizard otherwise cramped each pane to ~420-490px instead of a true 50/50 and gated live controls away. Re-parents existing .ctrl nodes (one source of truth), never mirrors; rail is hairline-only (Flat-Ink).

nodes.label: ADR-022: The platform design system is centralized into one root DESIGN.md; per-module DESIGN.shared.md deleted
nodes.rationale: Enacts ADR-010's waited-for end state: the four former design files merged into a single root DESIGN.md audited against live code (code wins), and the three DESIGN.shared.md copies deleted. Removes the drift surface (the copies had drifted ~2 lines); the merge also corrected stale doc claims (scale(0.97) press, 500ms/easeStandard dolly, solid-fill token). Supersedes ADR-010.

nodes.label: ADR-023: PRODUCT.md is centralized into one root file; per-module copies deleted
nodes.rationale: The two byte-identical per-module product contracts were audited and consolidated into a single root PRODUCT.md; both modules' CLAUDE.md now reference ../PRODUCT.md. Parallels ADR-022; removes the drift surface. The audit flagged two real gaps (Shift+arrow finer steps unimplemented; Module 1 mobile-notice wording diverges).

nodes.label: ADR-024: Topic-deploy folders are named graphics_module_<M>_topic_<K>_<slug> for the host catalog
nodes.rationale: Every deployed topic folder encodes subject-module index <M>, host-catalog order <K>, and a lowercase underscore <slug> so the host and a human can read catalog grouping/order from the name. Documents the rationale ADR-020 left descriptive; the numbers serve the catalog, not the master->deploy lineage (still the ADR-020 known issue).

nodes.label: ADR-025: A new subject module picks its template by geometry; Module 2 for 3D, Module 1 for 2D
nodes.rationale: For a whole new subject: if it manipulates 3D geometry copy Module2/ (the master, with orchestrator, rebuild pipeline, fat lines, mesh analyzer); if it is a sequence of 2D-canvas/diagram lessons copy Module1/. A subject fitting neither cleanly needs its own explicit architectural ADR before work starts; either template still consumes the root DESIGN.md/PRODUCT.md.

nodes.label: ADR-026: A sim's <title> in index.html must match the title field in meta.json
nodes.rationale: index.html <title> must equal meta.json.title: one human-facing name in two places. meta.json.title is the host catalog entry; <title> is the browser tab and the screen-reader accessible name, so a mismatch is both a catalog and accessibility defect. Topic 2 shipped a mismatch, fixed 2026-06-28. (Module 1 is seven pages under one meta.json, so per-lesson titles are by design.)

nodes.label: ADR-027: iShape.js is an adapt file, not a copy-identical shared file
nodes.rationale: iShape.js is adapt-on-copy, NOT one of the byte-identical shared files, because it carries topic-specific pose logic (the restingPlane VP lay-down quaternion, angleHP/angleVP inclination signs, explicit ZXY Euler). The master (4702 bytes) and topics (Topic 2 is 2652 bytes) legitimately diverge; copying it verbatim is a documented trap. The pure geometry generators next to it stay identical.

nodes.label: ADR-028: A new topic consumes the root DESIGN.md/PRODUCT.md, never a local copy
nodes.rationale: A new topic must reference the root ../DESIGN.md and ../PRODUCT.md via its CLAUDE.md and never create local copies. Makes ADR-022/ADR-023's centralization durable: every per-file copy is a drift point (the two DESIGN.shared.md copies had already drifted). A convenience local stub is just a copy that will drift.

nodes.label: ADR-029: Foundations adopts the orchestrator pattern + a per-edge line-of-sight hidden-line classifier
nodes.rationale: Foundations is rebuilt on Module 2's orchestrator pattern (superseding ADR-011 for this topic only), teaching BIS line types on an orbitable 3D Bearing Block. Retains meshAnalyzer.js and adds a net-new per-edge raycast occlusion classifier (lineDrawer.js) re-run on orbit (rAF-throttled). Module 2's convex normal.y>0 shortcut fails on the non-convex part; a Phase-3 depth-buffer attempt was reverted because it cannot draw dashed hidden lines.

nodes.label: ADR-030: Accelerate occlusion raycasting with three-mesh-bvh via the CDN import map
nodes.rationale: Add three-mesh-bvh (pinned, jsDelivr) to the same import map as three@0.160.0 to accelerate ADR-029's per-edge occlusion raycasts. A BVH turns each ray from O(triangles) to ~O(log triangles), the precondition for dropping the debounce (ADR-031). It ships as an ES module pinnable like three, so no npm/bundler/build (stays inside ADR-001). The BVH is derived state, rebuilt and disposed with the mesh.

nodes.label: ADR-031: Replace the occlusion debounce timer with real-time requestAnimationFrame throttling
nodes.rationale: The ~100ms occlusion debounce (recompute after the student stops moving) is removed; the visible/hidden reclassification now runs one pass per requestAnimationFrame, dirty-gated on real camera movement. The debounce only masked naive-raycasting cost; with the BVH (ADR-030) per-frame is affordable so edges flip visible<->hidden live. Establishes: heavy continuous-input updates are rAF-throttled + dirty-gated, never debounced.

nodes.label: ADR-032: The floating padded scrollbar pill is the platform scrollbar standard, tinted --color-border
nodes.rationale: Scroll containers show a floating padded pill (10px channel, 3px transparent border + background-clip:padding-box so only ~4px paints), tinted --color-border (~1.28:1). scrollbar-width is left UNSET on the base rule (only set inside a Firefox @supports guard) so Chrome 121+ keeps the ::-webkit-scrollbar pseudo-elements. Serves Visibility of System Status while staying quiet (Quiet Chrome); --color-panel was too invisible and --color-bench-grey too loud.

nodes.label: ADR-033: Module 1 fully adopts the orchestrator pattern, fully superseding ADR-011
nodes.rationale: Module 1's four remaining topics (Quadrants, First-angle, Points, Lines) migrate off shared engine.js onto Module 2's orchestrator + leaf-module pattern, each a standalone graphics_module_1_topic_* folder cut from the Module 2 skeleton. Quadrants+First-angle ship combined as 'Spatial Framework'. A platform-wide commitment, not a per-topic exception; fully supersedes ADR-011 and removes the two-architecture cognitive tax. engine.js is retired as a template.

nodes.label: ADR-034: The migrated Points Compare card draws its 2D sheet on one 2D <canvas>, not a second WebGL stack
nodes.rationale: graphics_module_1_topic_3_points honours ADR-012 but renders the Compare card's 2D orthographic drawing on a plain 2D <canvas> owned by the card's stage, repainted per rebuild, instead of re-housing the legacy second WebGL scene (S2/#c2d). A point's sheet is five primitives; a second WebGLRenderer would double GL contexts (context exhaustion is the most likely late-stage bug). Phase-6: now renders the PP lateral coordinate instead of centring it.

nodes.label: ADR-036: Restore the 3D-to-2D orthographic camera swoop during the fold
nodes.rationale: Overturns ADR-013's held-angle revision: the fold-to-flat again flies the front-on orthographic camera swoop with a perspective->ortho morph, landing square-on on the finished 2D sheet as the textbook prints it; the held-angle dolly (animateFoldHold) is retired. The held fold ended on a foreshortened sheet; landing square-on closes the 3D->2D loop in one move. Landed 2026-07-10 (animateFoldSwoop / swoopToAnswerSheet). The first reversal (camera does move) still binds.

nodes.label: ADR-037: The standalone Points Compare gains a true 50/50 workbench, in its own architecture
nodes.rationale: Brings Points Compare to parity with the Lines workbench (ADR-021): expanding Compare enters a true 50/50 split (wizard collapses, 3D left, 2D right, four point drivers docked in #workbench-rail). Built entirely in the topic's own code (DOM re-parent + body.compare-split grid + stepper.refresh), NOT via initSim cfg keys, which do not exist post-ADR-033. Re-parents existing [data-ctrl] wrappers; the 2D-canvas right pane keeps the single-canvas invariant. Strikes ADR-021's 'Points omits workbench' clause.

nodes.label: ADR-038: The 2D Compare orthographic drawing is a FIXED scale locked to the static sheet bounds
nodes.rationale: The on-demand Compare 2D orthographic drawing renders at a fixed scale locked to the static SHEET bounds (Lines: SHEET2D_SPAN=(SHEET/2)*10), so a real millimetre always reads the same on-screen length; it must not auto-fit. The orthographic sheet is a measured drawing; auto-zoom would shrink 10 mm as True Length grows and break the side-by-side comparison. ADR-014's clip-aware auto-zoom applies only to the 3D perspective main pane.
